items.q: What is the dancing banana meme?
items.a: It’s an animated pixel banana that waves its arms and dances — one of the internet’s first memes, created by Trym Stene in 1999. People also call it “the banana meme” or the “Peanut Butter Jelly Time banana.”

items.q: What is the dancing banana called?
items.a: A few names for the same 1999 GIF: the **Dancing Banana**, “the **banana meme**,” and — after the Flash version set to that song — the “**Peanut Butter Jelly Time** banana.” All the same dancing pixel banana I made.

items.q: What does the dancing banana mean?
items.a: It started as a “celebration” emoji — I’d post it whenever I finished something. These days it’s shorthand for pure joy, silliness, or “it’s [something] time!” energy.

items.q: Who made the Dancing Banana GIF?
items.a: I did — Trym Stene. I animated it in 1999 in Animation Shop. I don’t still have the original file as a smoking gun, but the story’s been picked up by USA Today, Fandom, City AM and others.

items.q: When was the Dancing Banana created?
items.a: Around 1999. I made loads of GIFs in those years, but this one shone the brightest.

items.q: Where did the dancing banana come from?
items.a: From me — Trym Stene — in **1999**. I drew it as a little “celebration” emoji to post on web forums whenever I finished something. It spread from there, and a later Flash version set to “Peanut Butter Jelly Time” carried it worldwide.

items.q: Where can I download the Dancing Banana GIF?
items.a: Right here, free — as the [original GIF or a transparent version](#download). No sign-ups, no watermarks.

items.q: Is the Dancing Banana the same as “Peanut Butter Jelly Time”?
items.a: Related, but not the same. I made the banana in 1999; later, others set it to The Buckwheat Boyz’ song “Peanut Butter Jelly Time” in a Flash animation — the song and that Flash are their creators’. That version even escaped onto TV: NBC’s *Ed* showed it in 2002, and in 2005 *Family Guy* put Brian in the banana suit. [Who made what →](/peanut-butter-jelly-time/)
Yes — I created it in 1999 and hold the rights. It’s free to enjoy and share for personal, non-commercial fun; commercial use needs a [licence](/license-the-dancing-banana/).

items.q: Can I use the Dancing Banana?
items.a: For fun? Go wild. For commercial use? [Read this first.](/license-the-dancing-banana/)
